- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.2) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast slightly.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points) — cap forecast at +3–4 points above recent peak.
- Model frequently underestimates mean-reversion trends — if recent 5-day average is rising, forecast should not drop below 1–2 points below that average.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings — smooth out forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before projecting.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.2–0.8), model often fails to capture gradual drift — adjust forecast to align with 10–15 day moving average of history.
